R' Eliezer (ben Hyrcanus) of the 9b.10 baraita
ת"ר (10a.2-3): EY created first, watered by God Himself, drinks rain water and drinks first
כי אתא רב דימי (10a.6), reporting the West
תנא (10a.8): מתמצית בית כור שותה תרקב

props.gloss_en: Ulla saw flying clouds (porchot) and said: put away the vessels, for rain is coming now
in the end the rain did not come
Ulla: just as the Babylonians lie, so their rains lie
Ulla: a basket full of honey [dates] for a zuz, and the Babylonians do not occupy themselves with Torah?
at night [the dates] pained him
Ulla: a basket full of knives for a zuz, and [yet] the Babylonians occupy themselves with Torah!
R' Eliezer: the whole world drinks from the waters of the ocean
R' Eliezer's verse: 'and a mist went up from the earth and watered the whole face of the ground' (Gen 2:6)
R' Eliezer: [the ocean's waters] are sweetened in the clouds
R' Yehoshua: the whole world drinks from the upper waters
R' Yehoshua's verse: 'it drinks water from the rain of heaven' (Deut 11:11)

R' Yehoshua: how then do I uphold 'and a mist went up from the earth'? it teaches that the clouds grow strong, rise to the firmament, open their mouths like a flask and receive the rain water -- as it says 'they distil rain from His mist' (Job 36:27)
and [the clouds] are perforated like a sieve and come and sprinkle water on the ground -- as it says 'a gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies' (2 Sam 22:12)
and between drop and drop there is only a hair's breadth
to teach you that the day of rains is as great as the day on which heaven and earth were created

the verses for it: 'who does great things without searching out' (Job 9:10) and 'who gives rain on the earth' (Job 5:10), and further 'the everlasting God ... there is no searching of His understanding' (Isa 40:28), and 'who sets the mountains by His strength' (Ps 65:7)
'who waters the mountains from His upper chambers' (Ps 104:13), and R' Yochanan said: from the upper chambers of the Holy One
the stam: R' Yochanan's reading of the verse runs like R' Yehoshua
the stam for R' Eliezer: since [the waters] rise up there, the verse calls them 'from His upper chambers'
for if you do not say so, 'powder and dust from the heavens' (Deut 28:24) -- how can that be? rather, since it is raised up there it is called 'from the heavens'
R' Chanina on 'He gathers the sea's waters as a heap, He puts the deeps in storehouses' (Ps 33:7): what caused the storehouses to fill with grain? the deeps
the stam: R' Chanina's dictum runs like R' Eliezer
the stam for R' Yehoshua: that verse speaks of the creation of the world
Eretz Yisrael was created first and the whole world afterwards -- as it says 'while He had not yet made the land and the outer places' (Prov 8:26)
Eretz Yisrael the Holy One waters Himself, and the whole world through an agent -- as it says 'who gives rain on the land and sends water on the outer places' (Job 5:10)
Eretz Yisrael drinks rain water and the whole world from the residue -- as it says 'who gives rain on the land' etc. (Job 5:10)
...and the whole world drinks from the residue
Eretz Yisrael drinks first and the whole world afterwards (Job 5:10) -- a parable: one who kneads cheese takes the food and leaves the refuse
the baraita's verse for its three watering contrasts: 'who gives rain on the land and sends water on the outer places' (Job 5:10)
the baraita's verse for EY's being created first: 'while He had not yet made the land and the outer places' (Prov 8:26)

R' Yochanan: it is written 'darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies' (Ps 18:12) and 'a gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies' (2 Sam 22:12): take the kaf, put it on the reish, and read חכשרת -- the waters' being made fit [is in] the thick clouds
in the West they say: bright clouds -- their waters are few; dark clouds -- their waters are many
the stam: what does R' Yehoshua expound from these verses (חשכת / חשרת)? he holds like what Rav Dimi reported from the West
the baraita: the upper waters hang by the [divine] word, and their fruit is rain water -- as it says 'the earth is sated from the fruit of Your works' (Ps 104:13)
the stam: that baraita runs like R' Yehoshua
the stam for R' Eliezer: that verse is written of the handiwork of the Holy One
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: the whole world drinks from the residue of the Garden of Eden
his verse: 'and a river goes out of Eden [to water the garden]' (Gen 2:10)
it was taught: from the residue of a beit kor, a tarkav drinks
